def: Splitting an answer into separate statements that can each be checked on their own.
A statement of exactly one fact, so that it can be judged true or false without the rest of the text.
Rewriting a claim so that pronouns and vague references are replaced and it makes sense with the surrounding text removed.
The relation that if the evidence is true then the claim must also be true.
The task of labelling a pair of texts as entailment, contradiction or neutral, used to check whether evidence supports a claim.
Whether an answer says only what the sources it was given say, regardless of whether the sources are correct.
Whether each statement in an answer is supported by the source it cites (the Attributable to Identified Sources idea).
A score for long text: the share of its atomic facts that a trusted knowledge source supports.
The share of answer sentences whose cited passages, taken together, entail the sentence.
The share of citations that are relevant, meaning they either entail the sentence alone or are needed because the others do not.
A verifier error in which a wrong claim is marked as supported, the most damaging error for a checking stage.
The verdict for a claim that the available evidence neither supports nor contradicts.
